Landscape Architecture & Design — Blue Mountains, NSW

Vibrant, inclusive and playful spaces that enrich communities and support local ecosystems.

The studio

Plateau Design is a landscape architecture studio in the World Heritage–listed Blue Mountains, working across the planning, design and delivery of landscape projects at every scale.

We are a small studio with a passion for projects that leave a big impact. We foster a collaborative, creative problem-solving approach to deliver complex design projects for our clients — from strategy and master planning through to documentation and construction.

We design on the traditional lands of the Dharug and Gundungurra people, and carry that responsibility into every site we touch.

Services

A comprehensive range of landscape architecture and design services, technical studies and reports, design review and stakeholder engagement — from first sketch to final planting.

  • Strategy, master plans & concept designStrategy reports, master planning, concept design and visualisations
  • DA packages & documentationLandscape DA packages, detailed design and construction documentation — hardworks and planting
  • Costing & construction phaseOpinions of probable cost (OPC) and services through construction
  • Landscape & Visual Impact AssessmentLVIA studies and expert visual analysis
  • Plans of ManagementPOMs and maintenance plans that keep landscapes thriving
  • Community engagementEngagement strategies and facilitation with the people who use the place

Experience

Plateau Design is led by Registered Landscape Architect Baz Richards. Before founding the studio, Baz gained over fifteen years of experience across Australia and internationally, holding design leadership positions at Sydney landscape architecture practices Context and Place Design Group, and most recently as Principal at RPS.

“For over fifteen years we’ve planned, designed and delivered complex landscape projects of all scales — new and upgraded parks, award-winning inclusive play spaces, and diverse urban spaces for learning and living.”

That experience now serves clients directly: principal-led design from the first conversation to the last tree in the ground.
